```{r}
library(DBI)
library(RPostgres)

con <- dbConnect(
  RPostgres::Postgres(),
  host = Sys.getenv("ADYN_POSTGRES_HOST"),
  port = Sys.getenv("ADYN_POSTGRES_PORT"),
  dbname = Sys.getenv("ADYN_POSTGRES_DB"),
  user = Sys.getenv("ADYN_POSTGRES_USER"),
  password = Sys.getenv("ADYN_POSTGRES_PASSWORD")
)
```

```{r}
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 1 AS connection_test")
```

```{r}
dbListTables(con)
```

```{r}
dbListFields(con, "customers")
dbListFields(con, "hormones")
dbListFields(con, "hormonevalues")
dbListFields(con, "resultvalues")
```

```{r}
dbListFields(con, "appointments")

dbListFields(con, "appointmenthistory")

dbListFields(con, "appointments_resultvalues")
```

```{r}
status_counts <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS appointment_count
  FROM appointments
  GROUP BY status
  ORDER BY appointment_count DESC
")

status_counts

outcome_counts <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT appointment_outcome, COUNT(*) AS appointment_count
  FROM appointments
  GROUP BY appointment_outcome
  ORDER BY appointment_count DESC
")

outcome_counts
```

```{r}
completion_check <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    status,
    appointment_outcome,
    COUNT(*) AS appointment_count
  FROM appointments
  GROUP BY status, appointment_outcome
  ORDER BY status, appointment_outcome
")

completion_check
```

```{r}
completed_appointments <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT DISTINCT id, customer_id
  FROM appointments
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND appointment_outcome = 'visit complete'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
")

visits_per_patient <- table(completed_appointments$customer_id)

table(visits_per_patient)
```

```{r}
completed_dates <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT appointment_date
  FROM appointments
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND appointment_outcome = 'visit complete'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
")

summary(completed_dates$appointment_date)
```

```{r}
duplicate_check <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS records_at_same_time,
    COUNT(*) 
  FROM appointments
")
```

```{r}
duplicate_check <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    appointment_date,
    COUNT(*) AS record_count
  FROM appointments
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND appointment_outcome = 'visit complete'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY customer_id, appointment_date
  HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
")

nrow(duplicate_check)

table(duplicate_check$record_count)
```

```{r}
View(duplicate_check)
```

```{r}
follow_up_counts <- dbGetQuery(con, "
```

```{r}
satisfaction <- dbGetQuery(con, "
```


```{r}
visit_counts <- table(visits_per_patient)

barplot(
  visit_counts,
  main = "Completed Appointments per Patient (Preliminary)",
  xlab = "Number of completed appointments",
  ylab = "Number of patients",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = NA
)
```
Of 44 customers IDs with qualifying completed appointments, 17 have one record and 27 have two or more. Most 31 of 44 have one or two, while a few have much higher counts, which include two with 36 each. 

This shows how common repeat visits are and how visits are distributed across patients. The preliminary repeat proportion is 61.4%, but possible test accounts and duplicate records could inflate it. It is not yet a validated retention rate. 

```{r}
barplot(
  as.numeric(status_counts$appointment_count),
  names.arg = status_counts$status,
  horiz = TRUE,
  las = 1,
  main = "Appointment Status Counts",
  xlab = "Number of appointment records",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = NA,
  cex.names = 0.7
)
```

```{r}
appointment_month <- format(
  completed_dates$appointment_date,
  "%Y-%m"
)

monthly_counts <- table(appointment_month)

barplot(
  monthly_counts,
  main = "Completed Appointments by Month (Preliminary)",
  xlab = "",
  ylab = "Number of appointment records",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = NA,
  las = 2,
  cex.names = 0.6
)
```
Appointment records peak in May 2024, with 83 records. 

This helps determine whether high appointment volume reflects many different patients or repeated activity from a few IDs. The May spike is concentrated, so it should not yet be interpreted as increased demand. Months with zero qualifying records are omitted from this chart. 

```{r}
monthly_summary <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    TO_CHAR(appointment_date, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS appointment_count,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS patient_count
  FROM appointments
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND appointment_outcome = 'visit complete'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY TO_CHAR(appointment_date, 'YYYY-MM')
  ORDER BY month
")

monthly_summary
```

```{r}
may_visits <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS appointment_count
  FROM appointments
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND appointment_outcome = 'visit complete'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND appointment_date >= '2024-05-01'
    AND appointment_date < '2024-06-01'
  GROUP BY customer_id
  ORDER BY appointment_count DESC
")

may_visits$appointment_count
```

```{r}
barplot(
  as.numeric(may_visits$appointment_count),
  names.arg = paste("ID", 1:nrow(may_visits)),
  main = "May 2024 Appointments by Patient ID (Preliminary)",
  xlab = "Patient IDs ranked by appointment count",
  ylab = "Number of appointment records",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = NA,
  cex.names = 0.7
)
```

```{r}
visit_dates <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT customer_id, appointment_date
  FROM appointments
  WHERE status = 'completed'
    AND appointment_outcome = 'visit complete'
    AND customer_id IS NOT NULL
    AND appointment_date IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY appointment_date
")

dates_by_patient <- split(
  visit_dates$appointment_date,
  visit_dates$customer_id
)

days_to_second <- sapply(dates_by_patient, function(dates) {
  if (length(dates) < 2) return(NA_real_)

  as.numeric(difftime(dates[2], dates[1], units = "days"))
})

summary(days_to_second)

hist(
  days_to_second[!is.na(days_to_second)],
  main = "Time to Second Completed Appointment (Preliminary)",
  xlab = "Days between first and second appointments",
  ylab = "Number of patient IDs",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = "white"
)
```
Among the 27 repeat IDs, the median gap between their first two observed appointment is 14.3 days. A few long gaps raise the mean to 69.7 days. 

This addresses how soon patients return, which adds information beyond simply counting visits. However, minute-long gaps require review, and the chart excludes IDs without an observed second appointment. 

```{r}
sum(days_to_second < 1, na.rm = TRUE)

short_gaps <- days_to_second[!is.na(days_to_second) &
                               days_to_second < 1]

unname(round(short_gaps * 24, 2))
```

```{r}
satisfaction_available <- c(
  Recorded = sum(!is.na(
    satisfaction$patient_interaction_satisfaction
  )),
  Missing = sum(is.na(
    satisfaction$patient_interaction_satisfaction
  ))
)

barplot(
  satisfaction_available,
  main = "Satisfaction Data Availability (Preliminary)",
  ylab = "Number of appointment records",
  col = c("steelblue", "gray70"),
  border = NA
)
```
Satisfaction is recorded for 61 of 219 appointments records (27.9%) and missing for 158 (72.1%). 

This chart shows a major limitation when comparing satisfaction between one-time and repeat patients: that comparison would cover only a minority of records and could be biased if ratings are recorded selectively. Also, 33 recorded values are zero. This chart shows data availability, not whether patients are satisfied.

```{r}
report_viewing <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_reports,
    COUNT(customer_viewed_date) AS reports_with_view_date,
    COUNT(*) - COUNT(customer_viewed_date) AS reports_without_view_date
  FROM resultvalues
")

report_viewinWh
```

```{r}
report_links <- dbGetQuery(con, "
  SELECT
    r.id AS report_id,
    r.customer_viewed_date,
    o.customer_id
  FROM resultvalues AS r
  LEFT JOIN samples AS s
    ON r.hormone_sample_id = s.id
  LEFT JOIN shipments AS sh
    ON s.shipment_id = sh.id
  LEFT JOIN orders AS o
    ON sh.order_id = o.id
  WHERE r.customer_viewed_date IS NOT NULL
")

nrow(report_links)
length(unique(report_links$report_id))

sum(is.na(report_links$customer_id))
```

“How should we identify real, completed patient visits and exclude internal testing, duplicates, or rescheduled appointments?”
We found test-like comments, conflicting completion labels, and appointments minutes apart. A reliable visit definition is essential for calculating visits per patient and repeat visits.

“What is the correct way to link a patient’s report-viewing date to their first appointment booking, and which timestamps should we use?”
This directly supports your goal of measuring the share of report viewers who book a visit and how long that takes. We need to confirm that the linked customer is the patient and that booking occurred after viewing.

“Where is follow-up recommendation information recorded, and how should we interpret the satisfaction fields?”
The follow-up flag is missing for all 219 qualifying records, and many satisfaction values are missing or zero. Clarifying these fields will help you assess whether follow-up recommendations and satisfaction are associated with repeat visits.
